readme: A seeded review set: extraction items over the frozen `report-calnext` excerpt,
some sound and some with a planted defect. `defect` is the answer key —
null means the item is correct and flagging it is a false positive.
Every quote is copied from the frozen fixture, so a verifier that actually
checks quotes against the document can settle most of these without judgment.
The reordered-quote item is deliberately NOT a defect: skill-tuner measured
small models reordering adjacent sentences inside otherwise verbatim text, and
a verifier that treats that as fabrication burns escalations on real material.

Items v-011 and up are generated from verbatim sentences of the frozen source with a defect planted mechanically, so the set scales past what is worth hand-authoring. Every quote is still real text from the document; only the paraphrase is manipulated.

items.why: Sound. Paraphrase matches, quote is verbatim.

item.text: The Technology Priority Maps give CalNEXT a framework for communicating priorities, defining focus areas, and screening projects.
item.direct_quotes: The Technology Priority Maps (TPMs) provide the CalNEXT program a framework to externally communicate priorities, clearly define the central focus areas, and assist with project screening.

items.why: Sound. A correct list of the partner organizations.

item.text: The HVAC TPM SME Team was reformed with representatives from each program team partner.
item.direct_quotes: with representatives from each of the program team partners: AESC, Energy Solutions, TRC, UC Davis, VEIC, and the Ortiz Group

items.why: The quote appears nowhere in the document. The cheapest defect to catch and the one the whole design rests on.

item.text: The report concludes that heat pump adoption tripled between 2023 and 2025.
item.direct_quotes: Heat pump adoption across the California residential sector tripled between 2023 and 2025.

items.why: The quote is verbatim, but the paraphrase attaches a figure the document never gives.

item.text: The HVAC category has changed more than any other, accounting for 62 percent of all revisions this cycle.
item.direct_quotes: The HVAC category has seen significant changes over the years, relative to other technology area categories.

items.why: The document has CalNEXT tracking while external programs lead. This reverses it.

item.text: Under the Observe role, CalNEXT takes the lead in unlocking these opportunities while external programs track progress.
item.direct_quotes: CalNEXT will track progress but encourage external programs to take lead in unlocking these opportunities.

items.why: The document defines Low as lower industry interest. This states the opposite while quoting the real definition.

item.text: A Low ranking marks the items with the highest industry interest and the largest Total System Benefit impacts.
item.direct_quotes: Covers items that have lower industry interest and/or impacts for Total System Benefit (TSB)

items.why: Not a defect. Two adjacent clauses of a verbatim passage appear in swapped order — a documented small-model habit, not fabrication. A verifier that flags this is costing escalations on real material.
